extracted.intended_audience: postdoctoral fellowship candidates (F32), their sponsors/mentors, and institutional officials preparing/submitting NIH NRSA Individual Postdoctoral Fellowship (Parent F32) applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and review criteria for preparing, submitting, and evaluating Ruth L. Kirschstein NRSA Individual Postdoctoral (F32) fellowship applications, including eligibility, required application components, and peer-review scoring considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will provide an overall impact score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood that the fellowship will enhance the candidate's potential for, and commitment to, a productive independent scientific research career in a health-related field, in consideration of the scored and additional review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score the overall merits of the application. Use the three review criteria areas defined below to evaluate the proposed fellowship application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate's Goals, Preparedness and Potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the candidate's previous educational, scientific and professional experience in terms of how it prepares the candidate for the proposed research training plan. Consider the context, for example, the candidate's stage of training and the opportunities available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the candidate and sponsor statements as well as the referee letters provide convincing evidence that the candidate possesses qualities (such as scientific understanding, creativity, curiosity, resourcefulness and drive) that will improve the likelihood of a successful research training outcome. Consider the candidate's potential to benefit from the fellowship research training plan and to transition to the next career stage in the biomedical research workforce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Training Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the rigor and feasibility of the research training project and how completion of the project will contribute to the development of the candidate as a research scientist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the goals of the overall research training plan and the extent to which the plan will facilitate the attainment of the goals. Discuss whether the research training plan identifies areas of needed development and contains appropriate, realistic activities and milestones to address those needs. Consider whether the sponsor(s), scientific environment, facilities and resources are adequate and appropriate for the proposed research training plan. If the candidate is proposing to gain experience in a clinical trial as part of his or her research training, evaluate evidence of the appropriate expertise, experience, resources, and ability on the part of the sponsor(s) to guide the applicant during the clinical trial research experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to Candidate, Mentoring and Training Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the sponsor(s) presents a strong mentoring plan appropriate to the needs and goals of the candidate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the extent to which the sponsor(s) and organizational commitment is appropriate, sufficient and in alignment with the candidate's research training plan. Consider whether the level of the commitment provided will contribute to the successful completion of the proposed plan and allow the candidate to advance to a productive career in the biomedical research workforce. If proposed, determine whether the clinical trial experience will contribute to the proposed project and/or the candidate's research training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: For research that involves human subjects but does not involve exempt categories, the committee will evaluate the justification for involvement of human subjects and the proposed protections from research risk relating to their participation according to five review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five review criteria: (1) risk to subjects, (2) adequacy of protection against risks, (3) potential benefits to the subjects and others, (4) importance of the knowledge to be gained, and (5) data and safety monitoring for clinical trials. For exempt research evaluate: (1) justification for the exemption, (2) human subjects involvement and characteristics, and (3) sources of materials. Refer to the Guidelines for the Review of Human Subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Human Subjects Policies
rubrics_metrics.description: When the proposed project involves human subjects and/or NIH-defined clinical research, the committee will evaluate the proposed plans for inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Guidelines for the Review of Inclusion in Clinical Research for additional instructions on assessing inclusion plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee will evaluate the involvement of live vertebrate animals as part of the scientific assessment according to three points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review points: (1) a complete description of all proposed procedures including species, strains, ages, sex, and total numbers of animals to be used; (2) justifications that the species is appropriate for the proposed research and why the research goals cannot be accomplished using an alternative non-animal model; and (3) interventions including analgesia, anesthesia, sedation, palliative care, and humane endpoints to limit discomfort, distress, pain and injury. Methods of euthanasia and justification for selected methods, if NOT consistent with the AVMA Guidelines, are also required. See the Worksheet for Review of the Vertebrate Animals Section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether materials or procedures proposed are potentially hazardous to research personnel and/or the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If hazards exist, reviewers determine whether adequate protection is proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmissions
rubrics_metrics.description: For resubmissions, the committee will evaluate the application as now presented, taking into consideration the responses to comments from the previous scientific review group and changes made to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the applicant addressed prior reviewers' critiques and improved the application accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewals (progress assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the rare cases where a fellowship renewal is considered, the committee will consider the progress made in the last funding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual fellowship awards are generally not renewable; when applicable, evaluate documented progress during prior support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications must include a plan to fulfill NIH requirements for instruction in the Responsible Conduct of Research. Reviewers will evaluate the adequacy of the proposed RCR training in relation to five required components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five required components: 1) Format — face-to-face lectures, coursework, and/or real-time discussion groups (a plan with only on-line instruction is not acceptable); 2) Subject Matter — breadth (e.g., conflict of interest, authorship, data management, human subjects and animal use, laboratory safety, research misconduct, research ethics); 3) Faculty Participation — role of sponsor(s) and other faculty involvement; 4) Duration of Instruction — number of contact hours (at least eight contact hours required); and 5) Frequency of Instruction — instruction must occur during each career stage and at least once every four years. Plans and past record will be rated as ACCEPTABLE or UNACCEPTABLE; the summary statement will provide the consensus of the review committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications from Foreign Organizations (scientific justification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether the project presents special opportunities for furthering research programs through the use of unusual resources, populations, or environmental conditions that exist in other countries and either are not readily available in the United States or augment existing U.S. resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign training must have clear scientific advantages compared to domestic training; justification will be evaluated in terms of scientific advantages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess the information provided regarding Select Agent research contained in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment includes: (1) the Select Agent(s) to be used, (2) the registration status of all entities where Select Agent(s) will be used, (3) procedures to monitor possession, use and transfer of Select Agent(s), and (4) plans for appropriate biosafety, biocontainment, and security of the Select Agent(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will comment on whether the Resource Sharing Plan(s) or the rationale for not sharing the resources is reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include Sharing Model Organisms and other applicable resource-sharing expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: For projects involving key biological and/or chemical resources, reviewers will comment on the brief plans proposed for identifying and ensuring the validity of those resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the applicant's authentication plans are adequate to ensure reproducibility and validity of critical reagents/materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will consider whether the budget and the requested period of support are fully justified and reasonable in relation to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether requested stipend, tuition/fees, institutional allowance and project period align with the training plan and scope of work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Completeness and Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications will be evaluated for completeness and compliance with application instructions by the Center for Scientific Review; applications that are incomplete or non-compliant will not be reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is critical to follow the Fellowship (F) instructions in the How to Apply - Application Guide and any program-specific instructions in the NOFO. Conformance to all requirements is required and strictly enforced. Use the specified submission systems (ASSIST, Grants.gov Workspace, or institutional S2S).

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS Fellowship Supplemental Form required sections
rubrics_metrics.description: The PHS Fellowship Supplemental Form must include Candidate Section; Research Training Plan; Commitment to Candidate, Mentoring, and Training Environment; Other Research Training Plan Sections; Additional Information; Budget; Appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow all instructions in the How to Apply - Application Guide and any NOFO-specific additions. Specific sections (e.g., Candidate Section Goals, Preparedness and Potential; Research Training Project Specific Aims and Strategy; Commitment to Candidate, Mentoring and Training Environment) have additional NOFO instructions to address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference Letters (required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant organizations must carefully follow the How to Apply - Application Guide, including the time period for when reference letters will be accepted. Applications lacking the appropriate required reference letters will not be reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference letters are submitted directly through the eRA Commons Submit Reference Letter link and not through Grants.gov. This is a separate process from electronic application submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page Limitations and Appendix Restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: All page limitations described in the How to Apply - Application Guide and the Table of Page Limits must be followed. Limited items are allowed in the Appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Appendix instructions in the How to Apply - Application Guide; any additional NOFO instructions are in addition to the Guide. Violations may lead to delays or rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor identification and commitment (application requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting the application, the candidate must identify a sponsor(s) who will supervise the proposed mentored training experience. One individual must be identified as the primary sponsor if a sponsor team is proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The primary sponsor should be committed to the candidate's research training plan and direct supervision. Candidates are encouraged to identify more than one sponsor if advantageous. If training is proposed at the doctoral institution, the application must document opportunities for new training experiences to broaden skills and knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: degree and immigration status at time of award
rubrics_metrics.description: By the time of award, the individual must have received an acceptable doctoral degree (e.g., PhD, MD, DO, ScD, etc.) and must be a U.S. citizen, non-citizen national, or lawful permanent resident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification by an authorized official that degree requirements have been met is acceptable. Foreign components and foreign organizations are eligible but must follow specified policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trial participation limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: This NOFO does not allow applicants to propose to lead an independent clinical trial, but does allow applicants to propose research experience in a clinical trial led by a sponsor or co-sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the candidate proposes clinical trial experience, the sponsor/co-sponsor must include a statement documenting leadership of the clinical trial including source of funding, NCT# and appropriate expertise. The sponsor/mentor is the responsible individual of record for oversight of the trial though fellows may participate in all components under supervision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of Effort (full-time requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time of award, individuals are required to pursue their research training on a full-time basis, normally defined as 40 hours per week or as specified by the sponsoring organization in accordance with its own policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NRSA fellowships may not be held concurrently with another federally sponsored fellowship or similar Federal award providing a stipend that duplicates provisions of this award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign Training Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual may request support for training abroad but must provide detailed justification explaining why foreign facilities/sponsor/experience are more appropriate than domestic training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justification is evaluated in terms of scientific advantages compared to domestic training; foreign training will be considered for funding only when scientific advantages are clear.
